title: Sapiom template manifest
description: Rich per-template detail, co-located beside each example as `template.json`. The registry (`registry.json`) stays the thin gallery list (id/name/description/tags/sourcePath/capabilities/steps); this manifest is the detail layer the Sapiom backend merges into the template + fork detail view. Everything is optional except `manifestVersion` — a bare `{ "manifestVersion": 1 }` is valid.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint pointing at this schema for autocomplete + validation.

manifestVersion.description: Manifest schema version. Only `1` is defined today.

url.description: Optional link to the author (site, profile, or repo).

whatItDoes.description: The card's lead paragraph — about three sentences. LEAD WITH THE VERB ("Create a cited account brief…"), never with the audience ("For turning a…"). Lived in registry.json until SAP-2076: it is detail-only data (`toSummary` omits it, only `toDetail` reads it) and was 25% of the thin index the shelf fetches, for prose the shelf never renders. It now sits with the other three sections of the same card.

longDescription.description: Markdown prose describing what the template is and how it behaves. Shown on the detail view under "About".

useCases.description: Concrete things you'd use this template for, as short noun phrases ("Relationship graph") — they render as chips, not sentences. Three is the house count.

notes.description: Markdown notes — how to use it, what else it ships with, gotchas.

examples.description: Sample runs: an input, and optionally the output it produces.

requiredSecrets.description: Third-party credentials the template needs. ONLY for credentials Sapiom cannot broker — never a Sapiom API key, never a non-secret value (use `settings`). Declares what the credential IS, never where it is stored: there is no `vaultRef`, no `connectorId`, no `store`, and there never will be. Binding `key` to a concrete value belongs to the resolver (`process.env[key]` today), which is what lets resolution move to connectors later without touching a manifest or the deploy panel.

key.description: Logical identifier the run reads. Must satisfy the engine's process-env rules: cannot be PATH, SAPIOM_*, or WORKFLOWS_* — namespace rules this pattern cannot express, enforced by the `manifest-secret-key` check in examples-check.

label.description: Human label for the input field.

provider.description: Provider hint (e.g. "slack", "notion"). NOT a storage location.

credentialKind.description: Shape of the credential, so the panel can label and validate the field.

description.description: Helper text: what it is, where to get it.

docsUrl.description: Link to the third party's token-creation page.

optional.description: True when the template degrades honestly without it — the run still reaches a terminal state and names what it skipped in `unmet[]`. False means the run cannot do its job at all.

settings.description: Non-secret configuration with a declared default, rendered as ordinary form fields and merged into the run input. Where a RECIPIENT or a lookback window belongs — NOT the vault, which cannot be listed, validated, or prompted for.

path.description: Dotted path into the entry-step input object this setting fills (e.g. `deliverTo`, `client.email`).

label.description: Human label for the form field.

description.description: Helper text shown under the field.

default.description: The value used when the user supplies nothing. REQUIRED — a setting without a default cannot support a zero-interaction run, which is the entire point.

example.description: A realistic value shown as placeholder text.

resources.description: Sapiom-managed resources the template provisions. Declarative so deploy can pre-provision and seed, and the UI can state cost and lifetime BEFORE a run — today every template does this imperatively inside a step, which leaves the setup panel nothing to render. Resources key on the PAYMENT ACCOUNT, not the definition, so without this declaration a resource cannot be attributed to a workflow at all; the best a panel could honestly say is "resources in your account this workflow can use".

kind.description: What gets provisioned. `setup.provisions[]` in the registry is derived from these.

handle.description: Stable lookup handle the step code addresses it by (`ctx.sapiom.database.get(handle)`). Unique within a template — two resources sharing one handle collide at lookup.

duration.description: postgres only, and legacy: the platform no longer reads it. A Sapiom Postgres is permanent and metered by slot — see the served rule at https://api.sapiom.ai/v1/agents/authoring-rules#database-lifecycle. Omit it in a new template; existing declarations still parse.

seed.description: Path, relative to the example dir, of a .sql file run once after provisioning so the first run has data to work with. READ-SIDE ONLY: seed a table the template READS. Never seed a table that is the template's own OUTPUT — fabricating rows a user might act on is worse than an empty first run. The file must exist; the `manifest-resource-seed` check enforces that.

ephemeral.description: True when the resource is disposable per run. False signals the template keeps state across runs and needs a durability story in `notes`.

key.description: The top-level entry-input key the run reads the chosen handle from — `resolveResourceHandle(input, { key })`, default `dbHandle`. This is the settings path the picker writes; a `settings[]` entry with the same `path` may render it as a plain field too. One key per resource is sufficient for the current gallery (one Postgres per template); the field is what makes a second Postgres forward-compatible without inventing a second naming convention. Not a dotted path — `resolveResourceHandle` reads a top-level key only.

reuse.description: Present ⇒ the resource is user-repointable: the deploy-time reuse picker may offer "use a database you already have", and the run opens the chosen handle instead of the declared default. Absent ⇒ the resource is internal state (not user data) and no picker is offered — the honest marker for a database whose contents a user should never be handed. Only ever offer the picker for a resource whose STEP CODE reads the injected handle via `resolveResourceHandle`; a `reuse` descriptor on a resource the code hardcodes advertises a control the next run silently ignores, which the `manifest-resource-reuse` check rejects.

defaultInput.description: The input a zero-interaction run starts with. Merged UNDER the user's input and UNDER `settings` defaults, so an explicit value always wins. Distinct from `examples[0].input`, which is documentation and may legitimately contain values that cannot work on a fresh tenant (a repo slug, a live sandbox URL). The runtime guarantee lives in code (`z.string().min(1).default("Sapiom")`); this is its declared, renderable projection — the UI cannot introspect a zod schema across a GitHub fetch — and it NEVER overrides code.

zeroSetup.description: The machine-checkable expectation for an unconfigured run. An expectation asserts that the pattern demonstrably ran and the output is honest about it — not that the result is production-grade.

terminalState.description: The terminal state a zero-input, zero-credential run is expected to reach.

expect.description: Assertions over the terminal artifact that prove the pattern ran.

path.description: Dotted path into the terminal artifact.

assert.description: Closed assertion vocabulary — anything outside it is a check failure, not a new operator.

narrative.description: One honest sentence for what an unconfigured run actually produces. Rendered VERBATIM on the shelf as `setup.degradedWithoutSetup` — must never imply a send that will not happen.

app.description: The dashboard this template ships, if any. Absent ⇒ a template without a dashboard, which is most of them; nothing else about the template changes. The source lives under `entry` in this directory and clones with everything else, so the adopter owns editable code from the first moment. `start` / `port` / `build` are exactly what an App Link bundle manifest stores — the publish step maps them straight through, with `entry` as the bundle root. A hand-maintained mirror of the backend's `templateManifestSchema.app` (Sapiom `template-registry.service.ts`): the two MUST agree field for field, because a block that passes here and fails there is silently dropped on the wire — the exact failure `requiredSecrets` shipped with.

name.description: The DASHBOARD's own name, not the template's — it is the preview card's heading under the template's H1 ("Insight report dashboard", not "Scheduled Metrics Report").

entry.description: Directory holding the dashboard source, relative to this example dir, with a trailing slash (`"app/"`). It is the subtree the publish step uploads and the working directory `build` and `start` run in — so `start` is `node server.mjs`, not `node app/server.mjs`. Segments are plain slugs: no leading slash, no `.`/`..`, no hidden directories. Must exist on disk; the `manifest-app-entry` check enforces that.

start.description: Shell command that serves the dashboard, run inside `entry` after `build`. It must listen on `port` and keep running.

port.description: TCP port `start` listens on. A real port: the bundle manifest cannot take anything else. Avoid 3000 — a local Sapiom backend usually holds it.

build.description: Optional shell command run once inside `entry` before `start` — `npm install`, a bundler. Omit it, or write `null` or `""`, when the dashboard needs no build step; the backend reads all three as the same thing. Prefer no build step: a dependency-free dashboard starts faster and cannot fail on an install.

preview.description: Absolute `https://` URL of a REAL screenshot of the rendered dashboard showing this template's own zero-setup output — never a drawn mock, never a live embed, never an empty state. Rendered by the detail page's dashboard card at 1200×760, so capture at that aspect ratio (`pnpm examples:app:screenshot <id>` does). `https` only, mirroring the backend, which rejects anything else as an injection sink rather than a screenshot; `http` would also be blocked as mixed content. Host it in this repo: commit `preview.png` beside `template.json` and point here at its `raw.githubusercontent.com/sapiom/sapiom-js/main/...` URL — the same host production already reads the manifest from. It resolves once the PR merges.
